title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rotary/rope optimizations
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: Improve inference throughput and tail latency for long-context workloads by upgrading attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 variants, adding fused QKV+transpose and fused rotary/rope ops, and updating kernel selection + scheduling logic. This PR combines kernel-level changes, scheduler hints, KV-cache layout tweaks, and continuous-batching adjustments to realize end-to-end gains. Summary of changes: - Introduce FlashAttentionV2 kernels with optional fused QKV transpose paths (gpu/kernels/flashattn_v2_*.cu). - Add fused rotary/rope application kernels to eliminate extra GEMM / mem copies for rotary embeddings (gpu/kernels/rope_fused_*.cu). - Extend kernel selector to prefer fused variants when hardware and model shapes match; add runtime fallback to v1 kernels for older drivers/hardware. - Update KV cache in-memory layout to be friendly to fused kernels (reduce strided loads). Migration is guarded behind a runtime flag and an opt-in model profile. - Scheduler changes: bias continuous-batching heuristics to group requests with matching seqlen/pad distributions; add per-stream kernel preference scoring. - Perf harness + microbench suites updated; new unit/integration tests added to validate numerical parity.
commits: 5 commits: 1) add flashattn_v2 fused kernels and tests; 2) fused rotary/rope kernels + parity tests; 3) kernel selector updates and policy scoring; 4) kv-cache layout change + compatibility shim; 5) perf harness + docs + rollout flag

bench_summary: Microbench results attached to perf harness artifacts show 12-25% throughput improvements and 6-15% p50 latency reductions for long context models on A100/H100. Improvements are largest when continuous batching groups similar-seqlen requests; smaller benefit for very small seqlen (<256).
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV and rotary/rope ops. Expect throughput improvements and reduced p50 latency for long-context workloads. Rollout controlled via runtime flag; default off for Dedicated until canary completes.
